easy.def: To be up on your legs.
examples: Stand up, please.
I stand in line.
The tree stood tall.

more.def: To be upright on your feet, or to be placed upright.
examples: Please stand when the flag goes by.
The old barn stood at the top of the hill.
Flamingos can stand on one leg for a long time.

easy.def: A bright light in the night sky.
examples: I see a star.
Stars twinkle at night.
Make a wish on a star.

more.def: A huge ball of burning gas far away in space, which looks like a tiny light in the night sky.
examples: The sun is the closest star to Earth.
On a clear night, we counted hundreds of stars.
Some stars are much bigger than our sun.
Draw a star.
The tree has a gold star.
She got a star on her paper.

more.def: A flat shape with five or more points.
examples: The flag has a white star in the corner.
The teacher put a gold star on my paper.
She cut a star out of yellow paper.
He is a movie star.
She is a singing star.
The star signed autographs.

more.def: A famous singer, actor or athlete.
examples: The singing star waved to the crowd.
He dreamed of becoming a famous movie star.
The soccer star signed shirts for the fans.
School starts at eight.
I start my book.
The race started.

more.def: To begin something, or to make something begin working.
examples: The concert starts at seven o'clock tonight.
Dad started the car and turned on the heat.
She started drawing as soon as she got the paper.
It was a good start.
The start of the race is here.
We ate at the start.

more.def: The point at which something begins.
examples: The runners lined up at the start of the race.
We read the start of the story and wanted to hear more.
The first day of school is a fresh start.

easy.def: One of the parts of a country.
examples: Texas is a state.
I live in a state.
California is a big state.

more.def: One of the large regions that some countries, such as Mexico or Australia, are divided into.
examples: Alaska is the largest state in the United States.
Which state do you live in?
Each state has its own flag.
The garden is in a good state.
My room is in a messy state.
Water in a frozen state is ice.

more.def: The condition that something is in at a certain time.
examples: Water can be in a solid, liquid or gas state.
The old house was in a poor state.
The park was in a clean state after the picnic.
State your name.
Please state your answer.
He stated the rules.

more.def: To say something clearly in words.
examples: Please state your name and age.
The rules state that no one runs in the hall.
She stated her answer clearly.

easy.def: To be in the same place and not go.
examples: Stay here.
The dog stays home.
She stayed in bed.

more.def: To remain in a place and not leave.
examples: Please stay in your seats until the bell rings.
We stayed inside because of the thunder.
The turtle stayed under the rock all afternoon.

easy.def: To live somewhere for a little while.
examples: We stay at a hotel.
I stayed at Grandma's.
They stay for a week.

more.def: To live or sleep somewhere for a short time.
examples: We stayed at a cabin by the lake for the weekend.
My cousin is staying with us for a week.
The travelers stayed in a small hotel near the station.
Hold the ladder steady.
The boat is steady on the calm lake.
Use a steady hand to pour the milk.

more.def: Firm and not shaking; also, not changing much.
examples: She kept a steady hand while she painted the tiny flowers.
A steady rain fell all day.
He walked at a steady pace for miles.

easy.def: To take what is not yours.
examples: The crow tried to steal my sandwich.
The squirrel steals seeds from the bird feeder.
The fox stole a hen in the story.

more.def: To take something that belongs to someone else without asking.
examples: The raccoon tried to steal food from the camp.
In the story, a thief stole the king's crown.
Squirrels sometimes steal seeds from the bird feeder.

easy.def: One movement of your foot when you walk.
examples: Take one step forward.
The baby took a step.
I heard a step in the hall.

more.def: A single movement of the foot when you walk or run.
examples: The toddler took her first step.
With each step, the snow crunched under his boots.
He took three steps back to see the whole painting.

easy.def: A flat place to put your foot on stairs.
examples: Sit on the top step.
The steps are steep.
Do not trip on the step.

more.def: A flat surface in a set of stairs where you put your foot.
examples: Mind the last step because it is a little loose.
We sat on the front steps and ate ice cream.
She counted twelve steps up to the attic.
The first step is to wash your hands.
Follow each step.
The recipe has four steps.

more.def: One part of a series of things you do to finish something.
examples: The first step in baking bread is mixing the dough.
Read each step before you begin the experiment.
The last step is to paint the model.

easy.def: To put your foot down and move.
examples: Step over the puddle.
Please step inside.
She stepped onto the bus.

more.def: To move by lifting a foot and putting it down somewhere.
examples: Step carefully over the slippery rocks.
He stepped aside to let the little girl pass.
Do not step on the sleeping cat.
The dog ran after the stick.
I drew in the dirt with a stick.
Birds built a nest of sticks.

more.def: A thin piece of wood that has fallen from a tree, or a long thin piece of something.
examples: We gathered dry sticks to start the campfire.
The hockey player swung his stick at the puck.
She stirred the paint with a stick.
Glue makes paper stick.
The tape will not stick.
Mud sticks to my boots.

more.def: To become joined to something so that it does not come off easily.
examples: Wet snow sticks to your mittens and makes good snowballs.
The stamp would not stick to the envelope.
Peanut butter stuck to the roof of my mouth.
I am still hungry.
It is still raining.
She is still here.

more.def: Up to this time, or even so.
examples: It was late, but the children were still awake.
He lost the game, but he still had fun.
Is the museum still open at this hour?
Stand still.
The pond is still.
The cat sat still.

more.def: Not moving, or quiet and calm.
examples: The still water looked like a mirror in the morning light.
Hold still while I take your picture.
The forest was still, with not a sound to be heard.

easy.def: To not move or go on any more.
examples: The bus will stop.
Stop at the red light.
The rain stopped.

more.def: To end an action or movement, or to make something end.
examples: The bus stops at the corner every morning.
Please stop talking so we can hear the song.
A fence stopped the sheep from wandering off.

easy.def: A place where a bus or train waits.
examples: This is my stop.
The bus stop is near.
We waited at the stop.

more.def: A place where a bus, train, or other vehicle halts to let people on or off.
examples: Our school bus stop is at the end of the street.
The train made a stop at every small town.
Get off at the next stop for the museum.
Read me a story.
I like that story.
She told a story.

more.def: An account of real or made-up events, told or written to entertain people.
examples: Grandpa told us a story about a talking fox.
The story ended with a happy surprise.
I wrote a story about a robot who loved to cook.
Draw a straight line.
The road is straight.
My hair is straight.

more.def: Going in one direction with no bends or curves.
examples: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.
The road ran straight across the flat plain.
She has long, straight hair.
Go straight home.
Walk straight ahead.
I came straight here.

more.def: In a direct line, or without delay.
examples: Come straight home after school.
The arrow flew straight to the target.
Go straight and you will see the school.
I heard a strange noise.
What a strange hat!
The food had a strange smell.

more.def: Unusual, odd, or not known to you.
examples: A strange light was blinking in the sky.
It felt strange to be at school at night.
The scientist found a strange new insect.

easy.def: A road in a town with houses.
examples: We live on a quiet street.
Cars drive down the street.
Look both ways before you cross the street.

more.def: A public road in a town or city, with houses or shops along it.
examples: The parade marched down the main street.
Our street has tall trees on both sides.
Shops and cafes lined the busy street.
The strong man lifted the box.
An ox is strong.
The rope is strong.

more.def: Having great strength or power, and not easy to break.
examples: The strong wind blew down a branch.
She is strong enough to carry the heavy bag.
The bridge is built of strong steel.
There was a strong smell.
The tea is strong.
The sun is strong today.

more.def: Easy to notice, with a lot of flavor, smell or force.
examples: The strong smell of onions filled the kitchen.
The tea was too strong for me.
A strong wind blew across the field.

easy.def: Not wanting to change your mind.
examples: The stubborn puppy would not come inside.
My stubborn dog will not take a bath.
Do not be stubborn. Try the peas.

more.def: Refusing to change your mind or do what others want.
examples: He was too stubborn to admit that he was lost.
The stubborn stain would not come out.
The stubborn mule refused to cross the bridge.

easy.def: Things that you do not name.
examples: I packed my stuff.
Put your stuff away.
There is stuff in the box.

more.def: Things or materials that are not named exactly.
examples: Put all your stuff in your backpack before you leave.
What is that sticky stuff on the table?
There is a lot of old stuff in the attic.
Leaving the door open was a stupid thing to do.
That was a stupid mistake.
I felt stupid when I forgot my own name.

more.def: Showing poor thinking or a lack of common sense.
examples: It was a stupid mistake to leave the gate open, and the sheep got out.
Running into the street without looking is a stupid thing to do.
He felt stupid after locking his keys inside the car.
